content.thinking:
I'm checking whether the model needs a root joint, planning to set one at the origin as the base of the structure before thinking through hinge joints for connected parts.

Now I'm sketching the concrete geometry: a swinging star pendant, armillary rings as hinge joints, overall body dimensions with width, depth, side panel thickness, plinth construction with stepped boxes and gold trim, all defined in terms of x/y/z coordinates for the front-facing silhouette.

Side panels become tall rectangles capped with pointed finials, with turned pilaster columns at the front corners topped by ornate capitals and cone-and-sphere spires. I'm defining the crown as a gothic ogee arch extruded between the columns, working out how to shape it as a tympanum slab with a cutout since simple outline extrusion won't give the right silhouette.

I'm sketching out the full height budget now—top board, gable slab painted navy with a gold rose-window decal, finial peaks, and whether a floating armillary orb fits above without making the piece too tall. Settling on shelf tier heights at roughly 0.16, 0.62, 1.06, 1.50, and 1.92 meters, with the gable peak around 2.45 and finials near 2.55 to keep proportions reasonable.

Continuing upward, tier 4 runs to the cornice underside at 2.34, with the cornice board, gable, and crown peak stacking up to around 2.8-2.9 with finials. This bookcase works well as the hero asset, so I'll skip adding a separate floating element and instead place the armillary sphere on top of it.

I'm reworking the tier math with five tiers of 0.36 height, pushing the cornice to about 2.18, gable to 2.50, and finial to 2.62, then figuring out where to put a wizard hat — rather than crowning the gable, I'll rest it on the flat shelf beside the gable on the cornice top.

I'm laying out the gable shape itself, with the peak around (0, 2.52) and flat shoulders on either side holding a candelabra on the left and the hat on the right, plus sketching the interior back panel dimensions for a painted navy starry backdrop.

For the stars, I'm using a cell-based noise pattern to scatter tiny bright dots across the dark panel, like pinpoints of light on indigo. Then I'm sizing the shelf boards with a gold trim edge along the front, and considering whether to add small corbel brackets or a decorative scallop beneath them.

For the side panels, I'm placing them at the outer edges with rounded front columns that slightly overlap the panel faces, and decorating the outward-facing sides with a gold vine-and-star inlay visible from a three-quarter angle. I'm settling on an overall cabinet width with the plinth extending slightly wider than the main body.

Now I'm skipping a bottom cabinet idea and instead planning the lowest shelf tier to hold large tomes—some lying flat in stacks, some standing upright, plus a bundled scroll. I'm sketching out the book-generation logic: each book gets properties like position, thickness, height, depth, color, lean angle, ornament type, and shelf placement, with standing books set back slightly from the shelf's front edge and their covers built as a box with an inset pages block.

I'm working out how the pages should be visually represented—since the spine faces outward and the fore-edge is hidden, the page color would mostly show as a thin strip visible from above between the covers, so I'm considering modeling the cover as separate plates with a slightly recessed page block rather than a single uniform box.

Triangle budget works out fine at roughly 3.4k for all the books combined. For tilted books, I'll rotate the whole geometry about its bottom corner, building a function that generates covers, pages, and spine transformed by a translation and z-rotation matrix. For lying/stacked books, I need to reorient so the spine faces forward, swapping which dimension represents thickness versus length.

For spine decoration, I'm placing a small textured plane just in front of the spine, tinted with colors like gold, silver, or teal, and reusing the same transform matrix so it rotates correctly whether the book stands upright or lies flat.

I'm sketching SVG spine designs with stripes and diamond patterns in a tall viewBox, accepting that the texture will stretch somewhat to fit each book's actual proportions—stripes handle the distortion fine, and circles just become slightly elliptical, which is acceptable.

I'll vary the design per book: double banded lines with a central diamond and dot, a title plate with ruled "text" lines, stacked rune circles with crosses and crescents, or a vertical vine with leaves—tinted mostly gold with some silver and teal accents.

I'm thinking through accessories: leather straps with gold buckles on the big tomes, a chained tome using a swept torus chain, a hero tome with a glowing rune gem and clasp, and an open book on a small wooden easel with glowing runic pages made from angled page slabs with ruled grain lines.

For the orbs, I'm planning a crystal ball on a brass stand with clawed spikes, using a glowing pale teal glass sphere with an inner swirling cyan texture to suggest magic inside.

Three orbs with distinct elemental tints—blue-teal for water, violet for void, amber for sun—each using an SVG swirl texture with stars, plus a small flattened white ellipse decal positioned on the upper-left for an anime-style specular highlight.

Now I'm designing an armillary sphere: thin gold torus rings mounted on joints like hinges, surrounding a small glowing core sphere, all supported on a stand, with each ring treated as its own bone-bound part.

I'm sketching out other shelf objects — a crystal ball on a claw stand, a celestial globe variant, and small gem/potion orbs — then moving into candle construction: a brass dish holder, a cream wax cylinder, drip shapes fused onto the side, a dark wick, and a flame element.

Writing flame lathe geometry...

I'm also planning a melted wax puddle beneath candles, plus a brass five-branch candelabra with a central lathe stem and swept arms ending in candle cups, placed near the gable shoulder along with a few extra candles elsewhere.

For scrolls, I'll build rolled parchment cylinders with darker tan ends decorated with a spiral pattern, tied with thin ribbon tori and finished with gold wax seal discs. I'm designing a diagonal lattice scroll rack with diamond-shaped cubbies holding scrolls that point outward, sized to fit the tier's width.

Actually, a diagonal diamond lattice is more distinctive than plain dividers—I'll build it from two sets of crossing slats clipped to the rectangle's boundaries so nothing overshoots the frame.

Working through the diamond lattice geometry...

I'm confirming the full lattice of rhombus centers lies at half-integer multiples of d where the coordinate indices sum to an odd number, then working out which rhombus center falls within the specified x and y region by tracking the tier boundaries.

Now I'm planning the detailed geometry: scroll elements seated in each rhombus center, slats cut at 45° with specific thickness and depth, and decorative crown gable details like an extruded ogee outline with gold trim swept along the edges. This is a complex model, so I'm working through building it piece by piece while keeping an eye on performance.

For the gable, I'm designing a glowing moon-and-star sigil — a crescent moon and surrounding stars rendered as extruded shapes with a soft glow, set against gold ring trim. I'm also planning gold finials with spheres atop the columns, and gold inlay textures with hanging tassels for the side panels.

Now I'm adding ornate gold tassels hanging from the column capitals, plus a navy valance with scalloped gold fringe draped beneath the cornices for that layered, decorative look.

For extra charm I'm planning a hanging star pendant with a chain and glowing crystal bead under the shelf board, and filling the floor with a vignette: stacked books, a candle, a glazed ceramic urn with scrolls poking out, and maybe a round rug to tie the grouping together visually.

The rug itself I'm giving a thin extruded shape with a painted concentric border pattern in gold and violet plus a star motif, sized to sit in front of the shelf and raised just enough off the floor to avoid clipping. Then I'll stack floor items like books on top of it, making sure their bases rest cleanly on the rug surface.

For the floor clutter, I'm adding stacked books with a dripping candle on the left, an urn with scrolls on the right, and a cluster of pillar candles on a brass dish in front. I'm also weighing whether to include a leaning library ladder against the shelf for added silhouette interest, positioned on the right side at a steep angle.

Tallying up the part budget across structure, books, tomes, scrolls, candles, orbs, ornaments, and floor pieces, I'm landing around 400 total elements, which feels manageable. For the palette, I'm settling on an anime high-fantasy feel with warm walnut wood tones, a plum-dark wood accent, and a rich indigo frame with gold trim.

Now I'm defining the full color scheme: violet-indigo lacquer with gold filigree for the frame, warm wood grain shelves, a starry navy back panel, plus glowing accents in aqua, violet, and amber, and a varied book spine palette spanning crimson, teal, emerald, plum, cream, royal blue, orange, rose, and dark tones, all tied together with a flat gold and shadow-gold finish.

Writing shading logic...

I need lathe parts bound to the correct bone -- with only one root joint, everything defaults there, but hinge joints could incorrectly steal nearby parts, so I'm writing small wrapper helpers that force bone: root unless explicitly overridden.

For model-space geometry I should always pass an explicit origin position rather than relying on joint placement. For things like flattened highlights, I'll scale a sphere geometry non-uniformly before placing it with position and direction to get the right orientation.

Now I'm working out the gable's extruded outline, defining it along the x-y plane with thickness running along z, centered symmetrically. I'm sketching the half-profile of the ogee curve as a series of points moving up from the base to the peak.

Still working out the ogee curve math...

Defining outline points for the gable's left and right edges from base to peak, then adding gold trim along the edge and small gothic crocket details spaced along the path.

For the crockets I'm placing small gold cone spikes pointing upward at sampled edge points. Then I'm designing a circular rose-window sigil on the gable face, centered above the base, with gold rings, twelve tick marks, a crescent moon, and tiny stars rendered as an extruded glowing emblem.

I'm also working out the gable slab's depth and z-position so its front face sits forward near the cornice, keeping the geometry simple and skipping a detailed rear finish since it's rarely seen.

For the back panel I'm sketching a plain navy board with a few sparse stars for texture. Then I'm laying out the cornice as stepped boxes with gold bead trim at the top tier, confirming tier 4's height lines up cleanly under it at 2.10, and starting to think through the column capital as a lathe-style sweep with a possible barley-twist shaft.

I'm considering giving the shaft an elliptical cross-section with a strong twist to create that spiral ribbon look, weighing the geometry cost in rings and triangles, and debating whether a twisted column actually fits the overall style.

I'll just paint the spiral stripe decoratively at roughly six turns per meter, independent of the geometric twist rate. Then I'll design tassels—gold cord loops with hanging strands—to drape from the front sides of the column capitals, four in total.

For the rug, I'm working out the extrude outline and paint function: a rounded rectangle border in navy with a gold line, a teal diamond-motif band, and a plum center with a radial star medallion built from angular rays. I'm mapping the extrude axes so the rug's horizontal spans correctly across the model.

Placing floor objects at y=0.02, then working out the tier shelf layout: each tier's board sits on stacked heights of 0.14, 0.54, 0.94, 1.34, 1.74 with 0.04 thick boards, and I'm reconciling how the bottom board meets the plinth top at 0.10.

For tier zero's contents, I'm sketching a casual stack of large tomes with a chained, gem-lit clasp, trying to fit either four tomes or three plus a candle within the 0.36 clearance.

Moving to the middle and right sections of tier zero, I'm placing a row of standing books and a violet crystal ball on a claw stand, checking that heights clear the shelf gap. Then for tier one, I'm planning leaning stacks of taller books on the left and considering a lectern or easel element for the center.

Continuing to map tiers: T1 gets books with a moon bookend on the left, a lying pair plus hourglass in the middle, and a potion-bottle shelf on the right; T2 has a scroll rack, standing books, and an armillary sphere; T3 starts with an open tome on the left.

For T3 I'm adding glowing-rune candle pairs, a hanging star charm underneath an upper board, and an inkwell with quill set on a small book stack to the right. T4 brings in tall slim grimoires, an amber orb on a stand, a small candelabra with candle stubs and flame, plus leaning books, while the top shoulders get a five-candle candelabra on one side and a wizard hat stacked on books on the other.

Now I'm writing helper logic to generate rows of books with randomized widths, spacing, heights capped under the tier limit, and occasional gaps or tilted end books, storing each placement by color. I'm also working out the transform math for tilted books, rotating around a pivot at the book's bottom corner to create a realistic leaning effect.

Confirming the physical lean: rotating clockwise about the bottom-right corner makes the bottom-left corner rise, which matches a book leaning right against its neighbor, with the top displaced rightward so I need to leave a gap there. I'll skip adding headband details and focus on spine textures for the gold banding.

For hero tomes, I'm planning corner decorations like small gold metal protectors, a glowing central gem, and a clasp, plus a generic lying-book function with cover plates, pages, spine texture, and a top-face gold emblem decal, keeping individual parts simple since there are only a handful of these.

Working out lying-book rotation math...

Working out plane sizing and texture orientation for the decal, then thinking through the general transform for lying vs standing books—applying yaw and a pivot-based lean rotation combined with position translation to build each book's full matrix.

Now I'm setting up the data structures to collect geometry by color and texture, then building the box geometries for covers, spine, side plates, and pages with specific thickness and offset dimensions...

Working out page recess depth so pages sit flush with covers but recessed slightly at the back, keeping triangle counts low across all 80 books, then thinking about the cream paper texture with a subtle grain pattern for the pages.

I'll skip the fine-grained page-line detail and just give pages a flat cream/tan cel paint. For covers, I'm layering a subtle leather-like mottle texture on top of the base color for a hand-painted feel, then moving on to counting painted areas and sketching out orb textures using SVG gradients with color bands and swirl patterns.

For the orb itself, I'm drawing the sphere texture as a double-wide strip so it wraps seamlessly, concentrating the swirl detail in the central visible region and keeping the edges plain for seamlessness. I'll add a white highlight glint for glass shine, then design a claw-footed stand with a lathed base and curving gold spike legs holding the sphere, ringed with small gems.

Now I'm sketching an armillary sphere: gold torus rings at different angles, a glowing teal core sphere, a lathed pillar stand, and a tiny orbiting planet with its own glow, all connected with hinge joints rotating about local axes.

I'm defining a candle-building function that takes position, height, radius, wax color, and holder/drip options, then constructs the holder dish, wax cylinder body, and a slightly lighter top melt-pool cap as separate geometric parts.

Still writing candle geometry... I'm adding wax drips as scaled spheres running down the sides, merging them by color group, then a thin wick rod and flame shapes built from lathe geometry, grouping all flame outer-glow and inner-glow parts together so the glow effect applies efficiently across many candles.

Now I'm sketching the candelabra: a gold lathe base and stem with five arms sweeping outward from the stem at varying heights to small brass cups, each holding candles of different heights, using curve sweeps for the arm geometry.

For the potions, I'm designing lathe-shaped bottles with round bodies and narrow necks, giving each a glowing solid-colored liquid inside, pale glass neck, brown cork, and a thin gold wire ring, in pink, green, and violet hues. Then I'm starting on an hourglass built from paired glass cones.

Rather than modeling transparent glass hiding the sand, I decide to fake the look: the bulbs themselves will be amber sand-colored lathe shapes (lower pile and upper reservoir), with the glass reduced to just thin rim rings around them, held between brass plates and three posts.

I'll paint sand color below the fill level in the lower bulb, and near the neck in the upper bulb's funnel, keeping the rest as pale glass — giving a stylized but readable hourglass surface.

Next I'm shaping an inkwell bottle with a gold cap and a quill, extruding a feathered outline with a gradient and zigzag edges for the plume. Then I'm building a wizard hat by lathing the brim and cone, sweeping a bent tapered tip, and decorating it with a gold band, small star decals, and a buckle in deep violet.

I'm positioning the hat on the cornice shoulder's right side, then adding a scalloped cloth valance below the cornice using an extruded outline with semicircular bumps, painted navy with a gold border and small gold beads or a tassel fringe at the scallop tips.

Front corner columns sit slightly overlapping the side panels, sized to align with plinth and cornice widths; back corners stay plain for simplicity. For the side panel decoration, I'm planning a vertical SVG filigree with gold vines and stars on the outer face, sized to fit the panel's depth and height.

Writing panel paint shaders...

Skipping candle glow effects for now. For the star charm, I'm planning a hinged joint with tiny gold chain links swept along a thin path, a star extrusion, and a glowing crystal bead, all as a bone charm. For the hero tome I want a hanging chain sweeping from the clasp to a shelf ring, plus a small padlock made from a box, torus, and keyhole, and a crescent moon bookend extruded in gold on a base plate.

I'm also adding small wizard clutter like a teal crystal cluster of bipyramid cones, brass nameplates with moon/star icons and gold studs along the shelf lip, and ornate anime-style silhouette details — finial spires, pointed gables, and spiral gold scrolls swept as corbel brackets under the cornice. Time to actually write the code now, which is going to be long.

Setting up imports and type-correct helpers...

Still defining paint colors...

Adding star color mixing and vignette shading near shelf edges...

I'm now defining the gold, brass, and silver paint palettes along with flat glow colors for the aqua, violet, amber, and flame accents.

Writing spine texture SVGs...

Still designing textures...

I also need an open book page texture with cream background, text line rects, illuminated capitals, mirrored for left/right pages, plus a glowing aqua rune overlay layer. Now I'm starting to write the actual file, setting up the builder with metadata and beginning the main build function.
